records.reading: Low rates until conditions are met
records.explanation: The Council committed to retaining the prevailing low rates until an inflation threshold was reached.
The answer clarified the contemplated direction after the purchases ended, without endorsing the number of increases priced by investors or specifying a first meeting.
The Council set out a further tightening path in its own assessment.
The Council set out a further tightening path in its own assessment.
The Council set out a further tightening path in its own assessment.
The Council set out a further tightening path in its own assessment.
The Council set out a further tightening path in its own assessment.
The Council set out a further tightening path in its own assessment.

This is a conditional tightening scenario, with unusually high uncertainty about whether the condition held. The written decision supplied a reaction function without direction. Protection of financial stability and the rate outlook were discussed separately.
The smaller increment allowed for evidence that policy was transmitting strongly. It did not imply that the Council considered the prevailing level sufficient.
The answer gave a clearer next-meeting direction than a general commitment to maintain restrictive conditions. No equally specific path was provided for meetings beyond July.

The label records the one-sided set of changes the Council contemplated. No probability was supplied for the hike relative to a hold. Coding this as an expected increase would overstate the statement.
The Council signalled a rate plateau conditional on the inflation outlook.
A hold conditional on transmission and inflation can be restrictive. Refusing to declare a peak leaves an upside risk without making another hike the stated path.
The market’s prospective cuts and the Fed’s discussion were raised by questioners. The Council supplied a duration assessment without announcing a date for easing.
She stood by her own earlier public remarks, but did not endorse the reporter’s description of a summer cut on the Council’s behalf. The holding signal was conditional on incoming evidence.
The Q&A opened a conditional path towards less restriction. June described when richer evidence would arrive. There was no agreed first-cut date, pace or size.
The Council identified circumstances under which it could ease further.

She declined to confirm a cutting cycle. One governor did not join the cut, but she reported agreement on deciding meeting by meeting. This is a conditional easing signal with a particularly uncertain pace.
These answers added directional information beyond the decision release. Neither the 25-basis-point cut just delivered nor a question about a larger cut established the size of the next move.
Two-sided inflation risks did not cancel the conditional easing orientation. The Council had not decided the next move or debated a destination for a neutral rate.
The answer supplied a baseline direction even though the release avoided a preset path. It gave no target for the cumulative cuts and no assurance that each meeting would deliver one.

A choice between a cut and a pause introduces easing as the one named direction. It does not mean a cut was more likely than a pause. Nor does the abstention identify a preferred future rate for the Council.

The time dimension and the explicit willingness to hold make this more informative than simply calling the present stance appropriate. It neither set a calendar commitment nor endorsed market pricing.

This was a conditional upward signal after a hold. The release on its own left the rate direction open. Further wage and inflation data, energy developments and changes in financing conditions could alter the assessment.
